name: Hugo Meisl
scopeNote: Hugo Meisl as Austria national team Verbandskapitaen/Bundeskapitaen/Teamchef, spell start 1913 (year only, partial dates for the excluded 1912-13 spell too, as decided by the user) to death 1937-02-17 (the death date comes from the brief; no fetched page gave the day, sources say only 1937). Style named by sources: 'Scheiberlspiel' / Wiener Schule / Danubian school ('Danubian whirl', 'Calcio Danubiano'), on a Scottish-derived 2-3-5 with a withdrawn centre-forward (Sindelar); coached with Jimmy Hogan's input. The popular label 'Total Football precursor' is retrospective. Meisl was chiefly an administrator (secretary, Mitropa Cup 1927, Coppa Internazionale, professional league 1924); how much he coached tactically versus selected the team is unclear. Almost all evidence is retrospective (tier C mirrors/press); no marking, pressing, transitions or set-piece evidence about Austria's own play was found.
openQuestions: Spell start: en.wikipedia says Meisl became coach in 1913 with Heinrich Retschury (full control 1919); profil says 1913 to 1937; ORF says his debut as Bundeskapitaen was 22 December 1912, a 3-1 win over Italy in Genoa. 1913 kept as decided by the user.

Meisl's own writing (articles, Mitropa/professionalism statements) was not found in any readable page; quotes in statedView are attributed anecdotes only. Next step: Franta/Weisgram biography, Willy Meisl 'Soccer Revolution', Wiener Stadt- und Landesarchiv, ANNO newspaper archive.
Austria's own marking scheme (man vs zone), pressing, transitions and set-pieces are undocumented in the pages read; only the opponent's man-marking of Sindelar (Monti, 1934) appears.
Tactical credit: Hogan (coach/trainer listed beside Meisl in 1931 line-up) versus Meisl as 'architect'; sources differ on who designed the style.
Jonathan Wilson 'Inverting the Pyramid' text itself was not readable; only a 2012 Wilson quote on Pozzo via Irish Times and a blog summary.

Austria-Forum states the birth of the Wunderteam (v Scotland, 1931-05-16) was gradual: seven regulars already played on 1931-04-12. Wikipedia en counts a 14-match unbeaten run from 1931-04-12 to 1932-12-07 while the Austria-Forum text says 12 matches plus 2.
Sources disagree on Sindelar's first cap/return (1923 untold game, 1926 Irish Times; 7 Jan 1929 dropped per Austria-Forum).

sources.title: Wiener Hugo Meisl als Urvater der EM (ORF Wien)
